key_insight: TIDER improves long-term agent memory retrieval by locating relevant time windows so temporally mismatched but semantically similar memories do not crowd out target evidence.
engineering_relevance: Memory-augmented agents can combine temporal filtering with semantic retrieval to better distinguish recurring, similar events across long histories.
method: Use an RL-trained 1.7B temporal interval locator to infer evidence windows.
Train discrete window selection with composite rewards derived from sparse answer supervision.
Merge temporal and semantic retrieval candidates, then rerank by proximity to the predicted windows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art accuracy of 61.52% on LifeBench (+8.82%) and 78.96% on LoCoMo (+3.66%).
watch_item: Incorrectly localized time windows could suppress relevant evidence; robustness to ambiguous temporal cues needs validation.
paper_title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
